**Description**
 Amazon’s global fulfilment network enables any merchant in any of the geography ship items that you order on Amazon, to any place on earth. Amazon Logistics’ (AMZL) delivery stations (DS) receive packages from Fulfilment Centers (FCs) and Sort Centers (SCs) and sort them to route level. Drivers come into the DS and pick up the packages for their route and deliver them to Amazon’s customers. This operation is also called the “Last Mile”. An integral component in the Last Mile ecosystem are Amazon's WW delivery hubs where packages are received, sorted and prepared for on\\-road delivery. Station Tech team, in Last Mile, is responsible for building scalable tools and technology for delivery hubs that scale across multiple programs and businesses including Amazon Logistics (AMZL), Global Specialty Fulfilment (GSF), to increase associate productivity, site throughput, and operational quality and scalability of our delivery network. Our primary customers are delivery station associates (our actual on\\-ground rockstars who sort millions of packages a day), station managers (who manage Amazon hubs WW to ensure customer promises are met), COs (central operations team who supervise stations across regions) and on\\-road delivery agents (drivers who sail through all obstacles to get your packages at your doorstep).  UTR Tech is an organisation within Last Mile supporting all the delivery stations in the delivery network. A delivery station receives an input set of packages from upstream and performs the required set of operations and processes on the packages to ultimately get them out of the delivery stations for on\\-road delivery. The associates within the delivery stations use a mobile based application called Dolphin for running the execution operations. As an SDE II on the UTR Tech team, you'll build and scale the systems powering Amazon's fastest delivery promises \\- Same\\-Day Delivery (SSD), Grocery, and Rush (1\\-hr/3\\-hr) programs across NA, EU, JP, and the Middle East. You'll partner with product, science, and operations to launch new speed programs and expand grocery (including perishable/chill\\-chain) into new regions. We're looking for an engineer who thrives on distributed\\-systems challenges at scale and wants their work to be visible to customers the same day.

title: GTM Engineer (Remote)
description:
**Read this part first** 





 Most GTM Engineer roles are a sales ops job with a new name. This one is not.
 





 BetterContact runs the waterfall enrichment behind modern outbound stacks. Scalantec runs the GTM systems of 25\\+ B2B companies. We are joining forces to build something neither of us could build alone: a company whose product is modern revenue systems. Enrichment, signals, agents and automation wired into one machine that takes a B2B company from noise to predictable pipeline, and takes their revenue somewhere they could not get to by hiring more people.
 





 That is the thing being built. It is being built for years, not months, and this is one of the first hires on it.
 




**How you will see it working** 





 In September 2026 we take the GTM World Tour to 10 cities across 2 continents in 4 weeks, Berlin to San Francisco. Every night, one real company's pipeline gets rebuilt live on stage in front of 60 hand\\-picked revenue leaders. No slides. No demo data. If it breaks, the room watches us fix it.
 





 The tour is not the job. The tour is where the systems you build get shown to the people who set the standard, and where the next hundred companies that need them are sitting in the room. Ten cities in September, more routes after that, and the work continues between every stop.
 




**What you will actually do** 



* Build enrichment and signal workflows end to end. Not run them. Build them.
* Take a real company's broken pipeline and rebuild it as a working system, then hand it over running.
* Turn what works into repeatable product. The one\\-off you build for one company in October should be the thing we deploy for twenty companies in February.
* Wire agents and AI into outbound where it produces a measurable lift, and cut it where it does not.
* Own the internal GTM stack for both companies and keep it faster than the market's.
* Prep and stress test the builds that go on stage, so nothing breaks that we did not choose to break.
* Write down what works. Half of it ends up in the GTM Manifesto that every attendee walks out with.



**The stack you will live in** 





 Clay. BetterContact. n8n or Make. HeyReach. Trigify. Claude and the current AI tooling. HubSpot or the CRM of whoever is on stage that night. If you have not touched one of these but you have shipped something comparable, that is fine. If you have touched all of them and never shipped anything that produced revenue, that is not.
 




**What we are looking for** 



* You have built GTM or automation systems that ran in production and moved a real number. Portfolio, Loom, screenshots, a Clay table, anything. Show it.
* You think in systems, not tasks. Given "our outbound is not working," you go and find out why before you touch a tool.
* You are comfortable with APIs, webhooks and data structures. You do not need to be an engineer. You do need to not be scared of one.
* You work independently, because we are distributed and nobody is going to check on you at 10am.
* Minimum 4 hours daily overlap with Central European Time.
* You want to build one thing for a long time. If you are looking for a three month contract, this is not it.



**What we do not care about** 





 Degrees. Where you live. Which company logos are on your CV. Whether you have had the exact title before.
 




**What you get** 



* Fixed monthly salary, competitive
* Full time, remote, work from anywhere. If you need relocation, we can support you.
* A long term seat on something being built from the start, not a role backfilled after someone left
* Direct work with both founders. Small team, no layers, decisions made the same day.
* Your work shown on a stage in ten cities to the people who set GTM standards
* Every tool you need, paid for, current versions



**How to apply** 





 Apply here. In the application, answer one question: describe one GTM system you built, what it replaced, and what number moved. Three sentences is enough. We read every one of these and it is the only part we score.
 





 No cover letter. Please.
